messages.author: 626730cd55a308d2
messages.subject: Which function generates regions.xls file?
parts:
Hi Henrik,
 
  I did paired copy number analysis using program on webpage with minor change and generate region.xls file.  I found this region.xls file somehow only contains information of chromosome 23, I rerun the program till: process(ce, chromosomes=c(1 :22), verbose=log);, but the region.xls is not regenerated.  What is the function i should use?
 
Also I am wondering if you have the answer to the following question I asked last time: is there a parameter like p-value to rank the possibility that if there is a true variation of copy number.  I did the analysis and check report with browser, some variations are certainly real and some are vague.  If there is a function that I can
extract one or several parameters regarding this (or if it can be included in region.xls file) it will be great.
 
Thanks you very much!
 
Yue
 
my program:

library(aroma.affymetrix);
log <- Arguments$getVerbose(-4);
timestampOn(log);
dataSetName <- "paired2";   

pairs <- matrix(c(
"H6VR08011701", "H6VR08011702", "H6VR08011703", "H6VR08011704",
"H6VR08011705", "H6VR08011706", "H6VR08011707", "H6VR08011708",
"H6VR08011709", "H6VR08011710", "H6VR08011711", "H6VR08011712",
"H6VR08011713", "H6VR08011714", "H6VR08011715", "H6VR08011716",
"H6VR08011717", "H6VR08011718", "H6VR08011719", "H6VR08011720",
"H6VR08011721", "H6VR08011722", "H6VR08011723", "H6VR08011724",
"H6VR08011725", "H6VR08011726", "H6VR08011727", "H6VR08011728",
"H6VR08011729", "H6VR08011730", "H6VR08011731", "H6VR08011732",
"H6VR08011733", "H6VR08011734", "H6VR08011735", "H6VR08011736",
"H6VR08011737", "H6VR08011738", "H6VR08011739", "H6VR08011740",
"H6VR08011741", "H6VR08011742"
), ncol=2, byrow=TRUE);
colnames(pairs) <- c("Tumor", "Norm"); 

library(aroma.affymetrix)
verbose <- Arguments$getVerbose(-8)
timestampOn(verbose)
csRawList <- list();
cdf <- AffymetrixCdfFile$fromChipType("GenomeWideSNP_6", tags="Full");
cs <- AffymetrixCelSet$fromName("paired2", cdf=cdf)
print(cs);
csRawList[["GenomeWideSNP_6"]] <- cs;

csAccList <- list();

cs <- csRawList[["GenomeWideSNP_6"]];
acc <- AllelicCrosstalkCalibration(cs);
print(acc);
csAcc <- process(acc, verbose=log);
csAccList[["GenomeWideSNP_6"]] <- csAcc;

cesList <- list();

cs <- csAccList[["GenomeWideSNP_6"]];
plm <- RmaCnPlm(cs, mergeStrands=TRUE, combineAlleles=TRUE, shift=+300);
print(plm);
fit(plm, verbose=log);
ces <- getChipEffectSet(plm);
cesList[["GenomeWideSNP_6"]] <- ces;

cesFlnList <- list();

ces <- cesList[["GenomeWideSNP_6"]];
fln <- FragmentLengthNormalization(ces);
print(fln);
cesFln <- process(fln, verbose=verbose);
cesFlnList[["GenomeWideSNP_6"]] <- cesFln;

sets <- list(Tumor=list(), Norm=list()); 

ces <- cesFlnList[["GenomeWideSNP_6"]];
for (type in colnames(pairs)) {
  idxs <- match(pairs[,type], getNames(ces));
  sets[[type]][["GenomeWideSNP_6"]] <- extract(ces, idxs);
  }

cns <- CbsModel(sets$Tumor, sets$Norm);   

ce <- ChromosomeExplorer(cns);
print(ce);
process(ce, chromosomes=c(1 :22), verbose=log);
process(ce, chromosomes=23, maxNAFraction=1/5, verbose=log);

> process(ce, chromosomes=c(1 :22), verbose=log);, but the region.xls is not
> regenerated. What is the function i should use?

Yes, the generation of region.xls using process() is a little bit
inconsistent.

You can use the getRegions() function for the CbsModel to calculate
it. For example:

cnrs <- getRegions(glad, arrays=1, chromosomes=22, verbose=log)

messages.subject: Re: Which function generates regions.xls file?
parts:
The reason you are getting these errors is that objects "cbs" and
"glad" do not exist in R's workspace, because you have not created
them. Comparing your code to the vignette on total copy number
analysis I am assuming you want to do something like

cnrs <- getRegions(cns, arrays=1, chromosomes=22, verbose=log) #
since cns is your CbsModel object, not cbs

You will also have to set up a GladModel object before you do
getRegions.

Ken

On 4/10/08, ken.m....@gmail.com <ken.m....@gmail.com> wrote:

The reason you are getting these errors is that objects "cbs" and
"glad" do not exist in R's workspace, because you have not created
them.  Comparing your code to the vignette on total copy number
analysis I am assuming you want to do something like

cnrs <- getRegions(cns, arrays=1, chromosomes=22, verbose=log)   #
since cns is your CbsModel object, not cbs

You will also have to set up a GladModel object before you do
getRegions.

Ken
